definitions.explanation: The number nine. Like four, nine has two readings: きゅう and く. きゅう is more common because く sounds like {苦|く} (suffering), making it somewhat inauspicious.

examples.english: I go to bed at nine o'clock.

examples.japanese: {九|きゅう}{月|がつ}から{学校|がっこう}が{始|はじ}まります。
{一|いち}から{九|きゅう}まで{数|かぞ}えてください。
examples.english: Please count from one to nine.

examples.japanese: {九|きゅう}{人|にん}の{友達|ともだち}がパーティーに{来|き}ました。
examples.english: Nine friends came to the party.

examples.japanese: {九|きゅう}{月|がつ}は{秋|あき}の{始|はじ}まりです。{涼|すず}しくなって、{気持|きも}ちがいい{季節|きせつ}です。
examples.english: September is the beginning of autumn. It gets cool and it's a pleasant season.

notes: Both きゅう and く are valid readings. きゅう is more common in general, but く appears in some fixed expressions and counters. The native counter is {九|ここの}つ (kokonotsu). {九|く}{時|じ} (kuji, nine o'clock) uses く, while {九|きゅう}{月|がつ} (kugatsu, September) uses きゅう in writing but く in the reading.
